description: Rust port of PyDESeq2's workflow (bindings/rust, examples/deseq.rs) against PyDESeq2 0.5.2 run as a black box with RapidGLM's inference back end (rapidglm.pydeseq2.RapidGLMInference), contrast = last design column. Produced by bindings/rust/tests/compare_pydeseq2.py.
commit_note: the source measured is this commit (v1.2.0-dev.1); it was made while the stages ran, and stages that started before it recorded be60928 with the same source uncommitted
timing_note: Indicative only: PyDESeq2 with 8 workers and Rust with 8 threads, both on CPUs 16-23. One workstation (Intel Core i9-13900KF, 125 GiB), 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-07. Four logical CPUs (8-11, on two performance cores) were offline after processor faults. Every timed run was confined to the 16 efficiency cores, one thread per core, because they are identical and the performance cores are not all available: one thread on CPU 16, four on 16-19, eight on 16-23, sixteen on 16-31. Timed runs held the shared timing lock, one at a time. Desktop services and a RAID consistency check kept every CPU about 7% busy. Another session ran untimed jobs on CPUs 20-31 at times; runs on those CPUs waited until other processes used less than a fifth of them, and the share others used during a run is recorded (others_cpu). Times on these cores are about 1.5 to 1.9 times those on the performance cores. Timings are provisional until the processor is repaired.
differences_note: Differences above 1e-6 come mainly from the dispersion trend, which PyDESeq2 fits by L-BFGS-B to a looser tolerance (trend coefficients differ by about 1e-5 relative); with PyDESeq2's trend coefficients injected (RAPIDGLM_TREND) airway agrees except genes with an all-zero design group (ill-posed fits). On thyroid32 the 42 genes with different missing p-values are Cook's outlier calls, from samples with leverage 1 (13 samples alone in their design cell).

cooks_leverage_one_thyroid32.note: Genes whose p-value is dropped as a Cook's outlier (missing p-value with baseMean > 0), against R DESeq2 1.48.2 run as a black box on the same design matrix. PyDESeq2 computes 0/0 at leverage-1 samples (infinite distances); the Rust port sets them to 0.
